scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc1 IP/netmask configuration
Mechanism: Server Room subnet is 1.0.0.0/8 (router2's eth0
  has 1.0.0.1/8). pc1 was configured with /30 instead of /8,
  confining it to 1.0.0.4/30 (hosts .5-.6 only). The gateway
  1.0.0.1 is OUTSIDE that range: the kernel rejects
  `default via 1.0.0.1` (nexthop unreachable), pc1 ends up
  with no default route and cannot even ARP the gateway —
  it is cut off from everything beyond its own /30.
Localization: pc1
Root cause: pc1 netmask set to /30 instead of /8 (gateway
  excluded from the local subnet; default route uninstallable)
Fix: restore pc1's mask and default route —
  `ip addr flush dev eth0 && ip addr add 1.0.0.5/8 dev eth0
   && ip route add default via 1.0.0.1`

agent.diagnosis_text:
The issue is with pc1’s local IP configuration (host networking stack). pc1 is configured as 1.0.0.5/30, which places it in the 1.0.0.4/30 network, while its intended gateway is 1.0.0.1. Because 1.0.0.1 is not in 1.0.0.4/30, the kernel treats the gateway as off-link and, with no default route present, immediately returns “Network is unreachable” for any traffic to 1.0.0.1 or beyond. Evidence: on pc1, ip addr shows 1.0.0.5/30 and ip route shows only 1.0.0.4/30 via eth0 with no default route; ping from pc1 to 1.0.0.1 fails with “Network is unreachable.” Meanwhile, router2 (the gateway on this LAN) is configured as 1.0.0.1/8 and routes 1.0.0.0/8 out of its eth0, confirming the LAN side is using a /8. This local mismatch explains why only pc1 is affected and others would not be.

Localization: pc1 eth0 IP/prefix and routing table. Mechanism: incorrect subnet mask shrinks the on-link network, pushing the gateway off-link; absence of a default route prevents forwarding to that gateway.

Root cause: pc1’s netmask was changed to /30 (and its default route removed) during maintenance.

Corrective fix: reconfigure pc1 to 1.0.0.5/8 on eth0 and add a default route via 1.0.0.1 (e.g., ip addr replace 1.0.0.5/8 dev eth0; ip route add default via 1.0.0.1 dev eth0), and make these settings persistent.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the fault to pc1 (pc1 eth0 IP/prefix and routing table) indicating a host-side issue.
The report explicitly identifies the incorrect netmask (pc1 set to /30 instead of /8) as the root cause of the issue.

Correctly instructs changing pc1’s netmask to /8 and adding the default route via 1.0.0.1 (and persisting the settings), which matches the expected fix.
